function.name: religion_history_get_councils
function.description: Retrieves a list of major councils in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the councils.

count.description: Number of top councils to retrieve.

function.name: religion_history_get_reformations
function.description: Retrieves a list of major reformations in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

count.description: Number of top reformations to retrieve.

function.name: religion_history_get_schisms
function.description: Retrieves a list of major schisms in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the schisms.

count.description: Number of top schisms to retrieve.

message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Year | Key Parties Involved | Main Cause(s) |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|---------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Eastern Orthodox Churches vs. Roman Catholic Church | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause, papal primacy), cultural and political tensions between the Byzantine East and Latin West. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Various European Protestant groups vs. Roman Catholic Church | Criticism of Catholic practices (e.g., indulgences, corruption), theological disputes (e.g., justification by faith), and the rise of vernacular scripture. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of 1965 (Ecumenical Dialogue)** | 1965 CE | Eastern Orthodox Churches vs. Roman Catholic Church | Efforts to heal the 1054 split; the 1965 *Act of Canonical Communion* was a formal step toward reconciliation, though full unity remains unresolved. |

These events are often cited as the “great” schisms because they reshaped the structure, theology, and political landscape of Christianity on a global scale.
